verdicts.strongest_argument: The finding concedes the two things that decide it. First, on publication: it describes its own source as 'pre-print coverage in this capture' that 'flags [the reversion] as overlooked, published two weeks before the print' - so the fact is in the captured feed, dated 2026-08-15T13:39:27Z in docs/766a040d...txt, complete with the two figures the finding quotes (6.5x forward earnings, 10.5% short float) and an explicit tradable recommendation: 'Long $82.50 or better, risk line $76. Jan 2027 $80/$100 call spread for a $920 debit.' A headline asserting 'the deadline Wall Street forgot' is promotional framing, not evidence that Wall Street forgot; and a licence agreement signed twenty years ago with a contractual expiry on 2026-12-31 is the archetype of structural-and-known - age is not novelty, and the expiry date has been fixed and disclosed since inception. Second, on mechanism, the hunter states it plainly: 'this is a January-2027 economic event: it cannot make this quarter's numbers, so its worst case is simply that it goes unmentioned.' A fact that cannot enter the reported quarter or the near guidance reaches this print only if management chooses to size it on the call, which is a coin-flip about commentary rather than an informational edge. Third, the finding's own tape works against it: the published recommendation was 'long $82.50 or better' with a $76 risk line, and the stock closed at 72.29 into the print after falling 16.97% over twenty sessions - the trade was stopped out, and the market that could read the article priced the stock 12% below the entry. That is not proof the reversion is priced, but it removes the finding's implied claim that publication had not been tested. Finally, its directional content is muddled: the hunter uses the licence upside as part of a net-negative read ('why my net number is negative rather than positive'), so the claim as delivered is not a signed bull case at all. I stop at 70 because I cannot verify from the capture whether sell-side FY27 models already embed the recaptured revenue - the two downgrades are relayed as headlines only, with no note bodies - and that is a capture limitation, not a concession.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Publishes the entire finding eighteen days pre-print: the twenty-year Calvin Klein women's dress and suit licences expiring December 31, the revenue coming home at PVH's own margin, 6.5x forward earnings, 10.5% short float, and a specific long recommendation with a Jan 2027 call spread.
A $3.08 Q2 EPS consensus with the correct 09/02 AMC report date was relayed in the same feed - so a consensus anchor for this print was public.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Spot 72.29 with run_up_5d -7.92% and run_up_20d -16.97% on 901,530 average shares - the stock fell through the published recommendation's own $76 risk line after the article ran, so the market saw the thesis and marked the equity down. Reaction history is punishing and already wide: eight prints, 10.81% median, only two up, worst -20.24%, so the baseline's expected move dwarfs a licence step-up that lands in FY27. Baseline is sound (fits_cadence, 8 events); no defective anchor is inflating this.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A dated pre-print sell-side FY27 model showing the recaptured licence revenue and margin were absent from published estimates, plus a quantification of the revenue involved - that would turn a known contractual date into a measurable estimate gap.

interactions: The claim, its consensus anchor, the JP Morgan downgrade relay and the CFO announcement all sit in one document (docs/766a040d...txt), so the finding and its own counter-arguments are a single source cluster rather than independent corroboration.
corpus_limits: PVH's capture carries no news items - EDGAR index plus a Stocktwits dump - so the BofA and JP Morgan notes exist only as relayed headlines and I cannot check whether either engaged with the licence reversion; the finding's core assertion that 'neither engages with it' is therefore unverifiable in both directions and is a capture artefact. I could not see the 10-K licence disclosures. No options chain, so no implied move or skew, and the article's Jan-2027 call-spread suggestion cannot be checked against actual chain pricing.
